text: This is Stack Blueprint.
Tell it what you want to build, and it plans the software and AI tools your coding agent needs.
For this demo, I want a silly mobile app where roommates photograph the fridge,
claim their food, and vote on suspicious leftovers.
A normal agent can suggest Expo, React Native, and Supabase.
Those are sensible choices, but it still has to guess how to use them well.
Stack Blueprint turns the stack suggestion into a shared plan.
With WebMCP, the agent sends the brief directly to the page, and the blueprint draws itself.
Stack Blueprint then searches Vibe Leaderboard, a maintained index of AI tools and agent-building advice.
Unrelated results are removed, leaving only what can help this project.
The software stack determines the AI workspace.
Expo adds Expo MCP, Expo Doctor, agent-device, and skills for project structure,
routing, and native user interfaces.
React Native adds Callstack's skills and React Doctor.
NativeWind adds the Expo Tailwind setup skill.
Supabase adds Supabase MCP plus database and Postgres best-practice skills.
These tools give the coding agent current documentation, project context, stack-specific patterns, diagnostics, and a way to test the running app.
Next, I ask why Expo was selected.
The inspection tool opens the same explanation for both of us: why it fits, its tradeoff, alternatives, and an official source.
Then I add a real constraint: keep Expo, but make the prototype work offline.
The agent applies this requirement to the existing blueprint instead of starting over.
Revision two keeps Expo and adds three pieces for offline work.
Expo SQLite for local data, NetInfo for connection-aware syncing, and an official Expo example to guide implementation.
It also makes the synchronization tradeoffs explicit.
Relevant engineering advice sourced from Vibe Leaderboard becomes instructions the agent can execute.
Define success before coding, keep context clear, review independently, and require proof from the running app.
The Stack Blueprint page registers seven WebMCP tools.
They use the same logic as the controls on screen, so the agent changes the actual page instead of returning another answer in chat.
Stack Blueprint gives builders and their agents one current, inspectable plan they can understand and improve together.
